answer: According to Section 136 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, if you assault or use criminal force on someone due to grave and sudden provocation given by that person, it is not considered a crime in the same way as other assaults. This means that if you were hit first and responded in self-defense, your actions may be justified under this provision, provided the provocation was indeed grave and sudden.
summary_answer: If you hit back in self-defense after being hit first, it may not be a crime if it qualifies as grave and sudden provocation.
detailed_answer: According to Section 136 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, if you assault or use criminal force on someone due to grave and sudden provocation given by that person, it is not considered a crime in the same way as other assaults. This means that if you were hit first and responded in self-defense, your actions may be justified under this provision, provided the provocation was indeed grave and sudden.
final_answer: It may not be a crime if your response was in self-defense due to grave and sudden provocation.
